subject.title: [Feature]: Memory durability config — hard flush threshold, priority-aware compaction, cache TTL

question: Should OpenClaw add public contracts for hard token-based memory flush, priority-preserving compaction metadata, and embedding-cache TTL, and should those land as one bundled feature or separate design decisions?
rationale: The issue asks for new public memory/config semantics in a subsystem where repository policy sets a high bar for config surface, durability behavior, plugin ownership, and upgrade safety.

options.title: Split Contract Decisions
options.body: Approve or reject hard flush, priority preservation, and cache TTL separately so each gets a focused schema, runtime contract, docs, and tests.

options.title: Accept The Bundle
options.body: Treat the three keys as one memory durability feature and require a broader design PR covering all schema and runtime surfaces together.

options.title: Defer New Config Surface
options.body: Keep current soft flush, safeguard compaction, and content-hash cache behavior until narrower failure evidence proves which public knob is needed first.

recommendation.title: Split Contract Decisions
recommendation.body: Approve or reject hard flush, priority preservation, and cache TTL separately so each gets a focused schema, runtime contract, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for both pre-compaction memory flush and embedding cache ownership points to Peter Steinberger.
